courses.subject: BEST
courses.title: Environmental Pollution, Monitoring, and Remediation
courses.description: This course aims to take students to explore the principles and current status of various global environmental pollution problems, which cover a range of chemical classes including legacy and emerging contaminants, environmental and ecotoxicological consequences, impacts on biodiversity, effective environmental monitoring, and pollution remediation technologies and application developments. The course will include basic concepts of environmental chemistry, ecotoxicology, ecology, ecosystem sciences, and environmental technology. Emphasis will be put in how these measurements can contribute to environmental sustainability. Pollution remediation technologies will be thoroughly examined through a number of large-scale case studies on their effectiveness.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Biodiversity, Environmental Management, sustainability and Technology
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students are expected to:

[1] understand the mechanistic processes governing global environmental pollution problems.

[2] understand the basic concepts and recent development in environmental monitoring and pollution remediation technologies.

[3] know how to design and conduct project assessing environmental pollution in solving some real-world environmental problems.

[4] know how to communicate with the environmental pollution sector with a scientific understanding of environmental pollution, and apply the concept to the pollution remediation and environmental sustainability.
courses.course_syllabus:
This course presents the recent understanding and advancements in global environmental pollution and their principles and mechanisms. The lectures are on a range of topics, covering fundamentals of environmental chemistry, ecotoxicology, environmental monitoring and remediation approaches, etc. Advanced concepts of application of environmental pollution remediation will further be discussed with a number of large-scale pollution mitigation projects.

| Week 1 | Course introduction, and overview of global environmental problems |
| --- | --- |
| Week 2 | Characteristics of diverse ecosystem types and their stressors |
| Week 3 | Fundamentals of environmental chemistry |
| Week 4 | Key classes of inorganic chemical pollutants |
| Week 5 | Persistent organic pollutants and emerging contaminants of concern |
| Week 6 | Principles of ecotoxicology and environmental hazard |
| Week 7 | Review and/or midterm exam |
| Week 8 | Global environmental pollution trend and environmental monitoring |
| Week 9 | Pollution remediation technologies in aquatic ecosystems |
| Week 10 | Pollution remediation technologies in terrestrial ecosystems |
| Week 11 | Future outlook of environmental pollution, regulation, and contribution to environmental sustainability |
| Week 12 | Project presentation and discussion (i): Case studies of an environmental problem, understanding, and solution |
| Week 13 | Project presentation and discussion (ii): Case studies of an environmental problem, understanding, and solution |
courses.required_readings: Lecture handout for each of the topics will be uploaded to the accompanied Blackboard site. Extra reading materials are expected to change every year to reflect the latest development in the research field in environmental pollution, monitoring, and remediation. Additional reading materials such as journal articles will be provided by individual instructor.
courses.recommended_readings:
1. Michael C. Newman. 2019. Fundamentals of Ecotoxicology: The Science of Pollution. 5th Edition. CRC Press. (ISBN: 978-0815354024)
2. Chaudhery Mustansar Hussain. 2020. The Handbook of Environmental Remediation: Classic and Modern Techniques. Royal Society of Chemistry. (ISBN: 978-1839161728)
